Rolling-origin backtest of a Timestral model

Source: R/backtest.R
timestral_backtest.Rd

Forecasts y from a sequence of forecast origins, each time using only the data up to the origin as the context, and scores each forecast against the h values that follow with timestral_score().

Usage

timestral_backtest(
  model,
  y,
  h,
  origins = NULL,
  initial = NULL,
  step = h,
  ...,
  level = c(80, 98),
  period = NULL,
  scale = NULL,
  keep_forecasts = FALSE
)

Arguments

model

a timestral_model from timestral_load()

y

the series to backtest: a numeric vector, ts/mts, zoo/xts, a matrix or data frame with time in rows, or a list of series (forecast as a batch at each origin; series of unequal length end together, see timestral_forecast())

h

forecast horizon in steps

origins

forecast origins as time indices (the last context step); overrides initial and step

initial

the first origin; NULL for the last five origins

step

spacing of the origins in time steps

...

arguments to timestral_forecast(): observation_mask, covariates (over the whole series), symmetric, clip_nonnegative

level

interval levels in percent for the coverage columns

period, scale

the scale of the scaled scores, as in timestral_score(); NULL period takes the frequency of a ts y. Each origin is scaled by its own context (a scale function gets the context up to the origin).

keep_forecasts

keep each origin's timestral_forecast in the "forecasts" attribute of the result (a list named by origin)

Value

A data frame with one row per origin, series, variate and step: origin, series, variate, step, t (the time index of the forecast step, origin + step), time (its time value, when y is a ts, zoo or xts), then the timestral_score() columns.

Details

Origin o means the context is time steps 1:o and the forecast covers steps o + 1 to o + h, so origins run from 1 to T - h for a series of length T. By default the origins are seq(initial, T - h, by = step); with initial = NULL the five last such origins are used (fewer if the series is short). Covariates and observation_mask in ... are given over the whole series and cut to each origin: past-only covariates and the mask to 1:o, known-future covariates to 1:(o + h), so known covariates need at least T rows. Steps the mask marks as missing are not scored either (their scores are NA). Forecasts are made one origin at a time, batching the series of a list y within each origin.

For tsibble data, use tsibble::stretch_tsibble() with the TIMESTRAL() fable model and fabletools::accuracy() instead.

Speed

With the native backend, a forecast reuses the work done on the leading patches its context shares with an earlier origin's context (a K/V cache; results are unchanged up to rounding, about 1e-13). Contexts are left-padded to whole patches, so two origins share patches only when they differ by a multiple of the patch size (m$config$patch_size, 32 for the official checkpoints): a step that is a multiple of it (or origins that mostly are) roughly halves the time on long series. The cache is not used when covariates are given (an observation_mask is fine), nor once a context is longer than the model's max_context, which slides the window.

Parallel use

The backtest is single-threaded, like the rest of the package. To run origins in parallel, split them and run one backtest per chunk, then rbind() the results. With forked workers (parallel::mclapply() on Linux and macOS) the loaded model can be used directly. Socket clusters and future workers are new R processes, where a model's native session is invalid, so load the model in each worker from its directory (m$dir), or use backend = "R". See the example.

Examples

m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
bt <- timestral_backtest(m, AirPassengers, h = 12)
unique(bt$origin)
#> [1]  84  96 108 120 132
aggregate(cbind(pinball, crps, ae) ~ step, data = bt, FUN = mean)
#>    step   pinball      crps        ae
#> 1     1  67.08972  70.15283 106.26091
#> 2     2  24.85504  25.81827  34.80820
#> 3     3  92.02138  95.27061 137.76800
#> 4     4  86.82393  89.57678 121.67124
#> 5     5 162.23108 162.64167 190.13702
#> 6     6 235.18160 235.38149 276.10486
#> 7     7 170.17754 173.56055 235.70929
#> 8     8 267.16880 267.12980 314.83744
#> 9     9 167.94929 169.04942 204.80626
#> 10   10  78.04683  81.29396 123.80253
#> 11   11  54.37409  56.83019  92.86966
#> 12   12  78.92028  81.83164 117.31144

# \donttest{
## origins in parallel on a socket cluster: reload the model per worker
cl <- parallel::makeCluster(2)
dir <- m$dir
origins <- seq(60, 132, by = 12)
chunks <- split(origins, seq_along(origins) %% 2)
parts <- parallel::parLapply(cl, chunks, function(o, dir) {
  m <- timestralR::timestral_load(dir)
  timestralR::timestral_backtest(m, AirPassengers, h = 12, origins = o)
}, dir = dir)
parallel::stopCluster(cl)
bt_all <- do.call(rbind, parts)
# }
